findings.F1: Daily moves reverse the next day, in proportion to the size of the move. Moves are measured in units of the coin's daily standard deviation within its window. After a fall larger than 2 of these units, the next day's return averaged +0.348 units (410 days, a rough t near 7). After a fall of 1 to 2 units it averaged +0.107 (1460 days), and after a fall of 0 to 1 unit +0.026 (6174 days). After a rise of 1 to 2 units it averaged -0.020 (1512 days), and after a rise larger than 2 units -0.098 (505 days). A third of a daily move is several times a round trip of 0.19 %, but the window-level scaling uses each window's whole history, so this needs a test on causal volatility.
findings.F2: The book's losses run through every coin and most windows. Its 938 trades lasted 28.6 days on average and lost 4.99 % each after fees (median -3.80 %), and only 34 % won. Every coin lost per trade, from -1.05 % on LTC to -13.46 % on XRP. 13 of 23 windows had a negative mean daily book return.

ideas.idea: A coin's return over the next day is higher the larger its fall over the past day was, measured against its usual daily move. After a large rise the next day's return is lower, more weakly.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean against a coin's sharp one-day falls, more the sharper the fall, and refuse to chase them with a short.
ideas.name: one-day fall reverses next

ideas.idea: When a coin closes below a falling Ichimoku cloud, its return over the next 26 days is lower the lower its 26-day return has been.
ideas.consequence: A trader would favour shorts below a falling cloud on coins still falling over the past 26 days, and refuse them on coins that have already rebounded.
ideas.name: below-cloud momentum keeps falling
